parts.text: Students are investigating the cooling of hot water in a beaker. They are using the apparatus shown in Fig. 2.1. Fig. 2.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Record room temperature θ R shown on the thermometer in Fig. 2.1. θ R = ........................................................ [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) A volume of 150 cm 3 of hot water is poured into the beaker and the initial temperature θ is recorded in Table 2.1. The temperature of the water is recorded every 30 s. The values are shown in Table 2.1.

ms.label: 2(b)(ii)
ms.text:
suitable precaution e.g.:
line of sight perpendicular to scale
wait until reading stops rising (at start)
stir before reading
keep thermometer at same depth

parts.label: i
parts.text: (c) (i) Calculate the average cooling rate x 1 during the first 90 s of the experiment. Use the readings from Table 2.1 and the equation x 1 = θ 0 – θ 90 T where T = 90 s and θ 0 and θ 90 are the temperatures at t = 0 and t = 90 s. Include the unit for the cooling rate. x 1 = ........................................................ [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the average cooling rate x 2 during the middle 90 s of the experiment. Use the readings from Table 2.1 and the equation x 2 = θ 90 – θ 180 T where T = 90 s and θ 90 and θ 180 are the temperatures at t = 90 s and t = 180 s. x 2 = ........................................................ [1]

ms.label: 2(c)(ii)
ms.text: unit °C / s, seen in (c) and not contradicted

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the average cooling rate x 3 during the last 90 s of the experiment. Use the readings from Table 2.1 and the equation x 3 = θ 180 – θ 270 T where T = 90 s and θ 180 and θ 270 are the temperatures at t = 180 s and t = 270 s. x 3 = ........................................................ [1]

ms.label: 2(d)(i)
ms.text:
cooling rate decreases (over time)
and justified by comparative values of cooling rate over suitable periods of time

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Give an estimate of the probable final temperature θ F of the water if left to cool for many hours. θ F = ........................................................ [1]

ms.label: 2(e)(i)
ms.text:
suggestion matching results
explanation matching suggestion:
EITHER:
SUGGESTION: smaller cooling rates (at equivalent times)
EXPLANATION: reference to cooling rate being smaller at lower temperatures and values stated
OR
SUGGESTION: smaller difference(s) in cooling rates (between equivalent times)
EXPLANATION: clear reference to (x2 – x3) being smaller than (x1 – x2)

ms.label: 2(e)(ii)
ms.text:
suitable control:
(same) volume of water,
(same) material of beaker,
(same) duration of experiment,
(same) room temp / named appropriate environmental condition
